problem: Existing semantically annotated 3D datasets of real indoor spaces are either room-scale (ScanNet, 3RScan, ARKitScenes, which has only bounding boxes), tiny (Replica with 18 scenes, Gibson-tiny), or coarsely and inaccurately annotated at building scale (MP3D). MP3D's per-segment and per-vertex labels give jagged boundaries, missed small objects, and semantic meshes misaligned with the RGB mesh. This limits training of embodied agents such as ObjectNav policies that rely on dense, accurate semantics.
motivation: HM3D provides 1000 high-quality building-scale reconstructions but has no semantics, and dense semantic annotation of such spaces is very laborious. The authors observe that scan-derived assets encode object boundaries in texture rather than geometry. Annotating in texture space therefore gives pixel-accurate instance boundaries without remeshing. They hypothesize that better and larger semantic annotation improves downstream embodied-AI generalization.
key_idea: Densely annotate 216 HM3D building-scale scans with texture-level, pixel-accurate object-instance and region (room) semantics (142,646 instances, 3,100 rooms). Then show that ObjectNav policies trained on this data generalize better across datasets than policies trained on Gibson or MP3D.
insight: Training on HM3DSem gives the best average cross-dataset ObjectNav performance for all three learning paradigms (Table 2). Average SR is 29.95 (RL), 28.86 (IL) and 47.70 (ML), versus 24.13 / 24.30 / 46.2 for the best alternative training set. With RL and IL, HM3DSem-trained policies even beat Gibson-trained policies on Gibson val (RL 32.96 vs 25.41; IL 28.02 vs 18.15), which suggests reconstruction and annotation quality transfers. Scaling matters strongly: RL SR rises from 17.79 to 39.36 as training scenes go from 25 to 145 (Table 3), and IL SR rises from 34.98 to 54.20 going from 25 to 80 scenes (Table 4). Mask R-CNN trained on HM3DSem renders reaches 31.8 detection mAP@0.5 on real ADE20k images, versus 14.5 (MP3D) and 1.1 (Gibson) (Table 6). Caveat: the comparison confounds annotation quality with scene count. MP3D-trained IL still beats HM3DSem-trained IL on MP3D val (28.57 vs 25.06).
method: Texture-space semantic annotation: artists paint unique hex colors per object instance into texture images on the original HM3D geometry. The result is packed as .glb, with a metadata text file mapping color to raw category name and region ID. Labels are also baked into per-vertex colors for simulator compatibility.

Annotation scope: covers architectural elements (walls, floors, ceilings, doors, stairs, split at room transitions), decor (pictures, vents, switches), furniture, appliances and clutter. Small items such as pillows, books and clothes are segmented where scan resolution allows. Raw free-form tags (1,625) are mapped to the 40 MP3D categories.

Verification pipeline: automated checks (colors in text match textures, each color used once per scene, file format). Manual validation covers typo and synonym consolidation and category mapping, plus virtual walk-throughs in Habitat to find missing annotations, messy boundaries, over-aggregation and mislabels. About 640 of more than 14,200 annotator hours went to iteration.

Dataset splits and statistics: 216 scenes randomly chosen from 950 furnished HM3D scans, split 145/36/35 train/val/test. On average about 660 instances, 106 categories and 14 regions per scene. Room types are inferred via object-category voting heuristics, with CSV statistics released.

ObjectNav benchmark: LoCoBot-like agent with 640x480 RGB-D, GPS+Compass, forward 0.25 m, turn 30°, look up/down and stop. There are 6 goal categories; success means stopping within 1.0 m of a goal instance with oracle visibility. About 7.2M train, 1072 val and 1000 test episodes. Adopted as the Habitat ObjectNav Challenge 2022 dataset.

Cross-dataset evaluation with three agent families. RL: DD-PPO, ResNet50 plus a 2-layer 512-D LSTM, 400M steps. IL: Habitat-Web behavior cloning with a ResNet18 RGB encoder, a PointNav-pretrained ResNet50 depth encoder, RedNet semantic features and a 2048-D GRU. ML: SemExp semantic-map exploration with Mask R-CNN and a PPO global policy, 10M steps. Each is trained on Gibson, MP3D or HM3DSem and evaluated on all three val sets.

setting.backbone: Three agent types trained per dataset: DD-PPO ResNet50+LSTM (RL, from scratch); Habitat-Web BC with ResNet18 RGB + PointNav-pretrained ResNet50 depth + RedNet semantics + GRU (IL); SemExp modular agent with COCO-pretrained Mask R-CNN + PPO exploration policy (ML)
setting.training_data: HM3DSem 145 train scenes (~7.2M ObjectNav train episodes) for RL (400M steps) and ML (10M steps). IL: 10k human demonstrations in the Table 2 comparison; scaling study uses up to 77k Habitat-Web human demos on 80 HM3DSem train scenes (~400M steps, ~20 epochs). Comparison agents are trained on Gibson and MP3D.

numbers_note: This is a dataset paper, so the 'methods' are standard agents (DD-PPO, Habitat-Web BC, SemExp) trained on HM3DSem. Table 2 also reports averages across the three val sets (HM3DSem-trained: RL 29.95/13.03, IL 28.86/10.66, ML 47.70/23.27). Scaling tables: Table 3 RL (Tiny 25 scenes 17.79/6.70, Small 80 scenes 26.87/11.18, Medium 99 scenes 35.16/14.90, Large 145 scenes 39.36/18.02); Table 4 IL (Tiny-HD 34.98/11.84, Small-HD 38.90/13.19, Medium-HD 48.32/16.07, Large-HD 54.20/18.71). The text cites Tiny RL as '17.70%' while Table 3 prints 17.79. Table 5 lists Habitat 2022 ObjectNav Challenge test-challenge entries from other teams (e.g. ByteBOT 64.0/35.0) plus a DDPPO challenge baseline at 25.0/12.0; these are not included as own results. Table 6 gives Mask R-CNN detection and segmentation mAP@0.5 (HM3DSem-trained: ADE20k det 31.8, seg 26.4). The HM3DSem val episode set (1072 episodes, 6 categories) is this paper's own and may differ from the later Habitat challenge HM3D ObjectNav v1/v2 val sets. How the Gibson and MP3D evaluation episodes were generated is not stated explicitly.
results: HM3DSem contains 142,646 annotated instances over 216 scenes and 3,100 rooms, which is 2.8x MP3D and 2.1x ARKitScenes by instance count. ObjectNav agents trained on it achieve the best cross-dataset average for all paradigms: RL 29.95 SR vs 24.13 (Gibson-trained), IL 28.86 vs 24.30 (MP3D-trained), ML 47.70 vs 46.2 (Gibson-trained). On HM3DSem val, SemExp reaches 55.6 SR / 30.7 SPL. Performance scales with training scenes (RL 17.79 to 39.36 SR; IL 34.98 to 54.20 SR). Adopting HM3DSem for the 2022 Habitat ObjectNav Challenge raised submissions from 400 (2021) to 1022.
limitations: Only 216 of the roughly 1000 HM3D scenes are annotated. Free-form tags contain many synonyms and residual errors, e.g. a refrigerator labeled as a cabinet.

Downstream evaluation covers only ObjectNav with 6 goal categories at low absolute performance. Gains mix dataset scale (145 train scenes) with annotation quality, and in-domain MP3D training still wins on MP3D for IL.
Room and region semantics come from object-category voting heuristics rather than explicit room-type labels.
